scenarios.expected: Allowed users can sign in and test mail reaches the controlled sink through the active configuration source. Invalid issuer/relay, denied domain, and locked environment settings have recoverable outcomes without exposing secrets.
scenarios.actual: Settings then Security then Authentication behaved as documented. In built-in mode the Magic-link sign-in switch was checked and disabled with the built-in-mode explanation. Removing an allowed domain left an existing Business User's live Portal session working but stopped her obtaining a new sign-in link, and emptying the list closed the Portal to that existing account too; restoring the domain restored delivery. An unreachable issuer was refused and registered nothing; a reachable issuer registered, displayed a callback URL ending in /api/auth/sso/callback on the instance address, and completed the pending switch to OIDC, after which the Provider ID was no longer offered. A colleague invited as Contributor completed a full browser round trip through the local identity provider authorization and the OpenLaw callback and kept the Contributor role. The Administrator retained password sign-in in OIDC mode while a Contributor using the same form was refused. Saving with a blank Client secret kept the stored secret and a further round trip succeeded; a pasted replacement rotated it; an unreachable issuer update was refused and left the working provider usable. In OIDC mode the magic-link switch was editable: turned off, the Portal entry page read "Sign-in links are switched off" and handed off to Sign in and Continue with single sign-on, through which an existing Business User still entered. Selecting Built-in restored the mode, switched magic links back on and locked the switch again, and a real sign-in link was delivered. Supplemental scope check: removing a domain refuses new magic-link issuance for everyone on it, including existing Business Users, while a held session, an already-issued unused link, and single sign-on for an existing identity-provider account all still work; an unknown address is still refused both routes. The Portal-entry section now states that scope explicitly. Wording clarification only, no new walkthrough: the retained-link and single sign-on statements are now explicitly scoped to existing accounts, because user.create.before still applies the allowlist to a never-created identity redeeming its first link, and the closing instruction now separates archival, which prevents new sign-ins and revokes existing sessions, from Revoke all sessions, after which the active account can sign in again. Both effects rest on the already recorded offboarding and scope observations.

scenarios.actual: Operator responsibility was performed with deployment tools against the owned fixture, not through a separate app role. Three immutable overlay phases were applied to the owned app and worker only, each recorded with its exact configuration hash and application time: phase env (review-phase-env.json sha256 55d555a132d1099704fd5da7b8f6c469191b55e1b7ebab0e40da91d4e56f1e82) set SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM, which made the wizard relay read-only, removed Save relay and Clear relay, and sent a real invitation whose envelope From was the environment sender rather than the stored one; phase incomplete (review-phase-incomplete.json sha256 ba55151ccfca66a9b666e9e65b9b8169c91b480deb1abd36a89c679d761599eb) set SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM, which held the resolved source at env with a null from address and produced no message at all despite a complete stored relay; removing the overlay and recreating app and worker returned the pane to "Outbound email is set in the app." and delivered a test message from the stored sender. Clear relay then moved the source to unset and stopped delivery until a valid replacement was saved. The frozen snapshot, source/.env and base overlay.json hashes were checked before every phase and never modified. Supplemental scope check: removing a domain refuses new magic-link issuance for everyone on it, including existing Business Users, while a held session, an already-issued unused link, and single sign-on for an existing identity-provider account all still work; an unknown address is still refused both routes. The Portal-entry section now states that scope explicitly. Wording clarification only, no new walkthrough: the retained-link and single sign-on statements are now explicitly scoped to existing accounts, because user.create.before still applies the allowlist to a never-created identity redeeming its first link, and the closing instruction now separates archival, which prevents new sign-ins and revokes existing sessions, from Revoke all sessions, after which the active account can sign in again. limitations: Independent walkthroughs are agent walkthroughs, not human user studies or feature-owner approval.

Single sign-on was verified against a dedicated local OpenID Connect fixture. It is not certification of a real provider's client-secret handling or account policy, and it does not satisfy the real DocuSign and AI-provider verification required by DOC-022.

Onboarding completion is instance-wide and irreversible, so one instance permits one finishing action. Set up later on the final invitation step was exercised; Finish and the Welcome-step Set up later were not independently exercised here.
Evidence was taken on fixture app commit 6a8873dbda333fd9992eb77525d4bfa3f47af20d, not the final app candidate. DOC-025 reconciles the catalog against that candidate.
Operator and module configuration guides remain forward publication dependencies.
